b2-marslakok-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Martians Anecdote
b2-marslakok-01.scenario: At a science evening in Budapest, a guest named Dóra asks you where the nickname 'Martians' for Budapest's scientists comes from.
b2-marslakok-01.prompt: Tell Dóra the anecdote behind the nickname.
cues: Say what Fermi asked and how Szilárd is said to have answered
Say what happened the deeper people looked into modern physics
b2-marslakok-01.target: A történet szerint Fermi azt kérdezte, hol vannak a földönkívüliek, Szilárd Leó pedig azt felelte, hogy már itt élnek közöttünk, csak magyaroknak nevezik magukat. Minél mélyebben vizsgálták a fizikát, annál gyakrabban találkoztak budapesti tudósok nevével.
b2-marslakok-01.english: According to the story, Fermi asked where the extraterrestrials are, and Leó Szilárd answered that they already live among us, they just call themselves Hungarians. The more deeply they examined physics, the more often they came across the names of Budapest scientists.
b2-marslakok-01.canDo: I can retell the anecdote about the 'Martians of Budapest' that is attributed to Enrico Fermi and Leó Szilárd.

b2-marslakok-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Neumann's Big Idea
b2-marslakok-02.scenario: After a talk at a Budapest university, a student named Bence asks you why János Neumann is still famous.
b2-marslakok-02.prompt: Explain to Bence what Neumann proposed for computers and what he did in game theory.
cues: Say where the program's instructions should be stored
Say what Neumann worked out together with Morgenstern
b2-marslakok-02.target: Neumann János az 1945-ös tervezetben azt javasolta, hogy a gép a program utasításait ugyanabban a memóriában tárolja, mint az adatokat. Amennyiben a program a memóriában van, a gép átkábelezés nélkül is működik. Oskar Morgensternnel közösen kidolgozta a játékelmélet alapjait.
b2-marslakok-02.english: In the 1945 draft János Neumann proposed that the machine store the program's instructions in the same memory as the data. Provided that the program is in memory, the machine works even without rewiring. Together with Oskar Morgenstern he worked out the foundations of game theory.
b2-marslakok-02.canDo: I can explain John von Neumann's contributions to stored-program computer architecture and game theory.

b2-marslakok-03.title: Communicative Challenge: An Idea at a Traffic Light
b2-marslakok-03.scenario: In a history class, a teacher named Kálmán asks you to tell the class about Leó Szilárd's idea in London and his letter.
b2-marslakok-03.prompt: Tell Kálmán what Szilárd realised in London and what he did with his patent and the letter.
cues: Say what became possible according to Szilárd's idea
Say on what condition he handed over the patent
Say who signed the letter and to whom it went
b2-marslakok-03.target: Szilárd Leó Londonban ismerte fel, hogy önfenntartó láncreakció jöhet létre. A szabadalmat azzal a feltétellel engedte át a brit Admiralitásnak, hogy szigorúan titkosítják. Ő fogalmazta meg a levelet, amelyet Einstein írt alá Roosevelt elnöknek.
b2-marslakok-03.english: Leó Szilárd realised in London that a self-sustaining chain reaction can come about. He handed the patent to the British Admiralty on the condition that it be strictly classified. He drafted the letter that Einstein signed to President Roosevelt.
b2-marslakok-03.canDo: I can recount Leó Szilárd's realization of the nuclear chain reaction in London and the Einstein–Szilárd letter.

b2-marslakok-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Wigner and the Edge of Space
b2-marslakok-04.scenario: At a school science club in Budapest, a member named Réka asks you what Wigner and Kármán are known for.
b2-marslakok-04.prompt: Tell Réka what Wigner and Kármán are known for.
cues: Say how Wigner described particles and nuclei and what he received in 1963
Say what the line at a hundred kilometres is called today
b2-marslakok-04.target: Wigner Jenő a szimmetriaelvek segítségével írta le az atommagok viselkedését, és 1963-ban megosztott fizikai Nobel-díjat kapott. Kármán Tódor kutatásai nagyban meghatározták a hangsebesség feletti repülést, és a világűr határát ma Kármán-vonalnak nevezik.
b2-marslakok-04.english: With the help of symmetry principles Jenő Wigner described the behaviour of atomic nuclei, and in 1963 he received a shared Nobel Prize in Physics. Tódor Kármán's research shaped flight above the speed of sound to such an extent that the boundary of space is called the Kármán line today.
b2-marslakok-04.canDo: I can describe Jenő Wigner's work on symmetry principles and Tódor Kármán's work in supersonic aerodynamics.

b2-marslakok-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Why These Schools?
b2-marslakok-05.scenario: A history teacher named Ilona asks you why so many famous scientists came from the same few Budapest schools.
b2-marslakok-05.prompt: Tell Ilona what the schools expected of their pupils and what happened when pupils had more freedom to ask questions.
cues: Say what the teachers expected instead of cramming
Say what happened the more freedom the pupils got
b2-marslakok-05.target: A visszaemlékezések szerint a híres gimnáziumokban nem magolást, hanem önálló gondolkodást vártak el. Minél nagyobb szabadságot kaptak a diákok a kérdezésben, annál bátrabban lépték át a tankönyvek határait.
b2-marslakok-05.english: According to recollections, the famous grammar schools expected independent thinking, not cramming. The more freedom the pupils got in asking questions, the more boldly they stepped beyond the boundaries of the textbooks.
b2-marslakok-05.canDo: I can discuss why turn-of-the-century Budapest secondary schools (Fasori, Minta, Reál) are said to have produced so many world-class scientists.

b2-marslakok-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Four Scientists, Four Fields
b2-marslakok-consolidation.scenario: At the end-of-year evening of a physics club in Budapest, the club leader, Mr Antal, asks you to say what each of the four scientists is known for.
b2-marslakok-consolidation.prompt: Tell Mr Antal one thing each of the four scientists studied, and what we gain from knowing more about them.
cues: Name a field for each of Neumann, Szilárd, Wigner and Kármán
Say that the more we know about them, the better we understand the century
b2-marslakok-consolidation.target: Neumann János a tárolt programot, Szilárd Leó a láncreakciót, Wigner Jenő a szimmetriaelveket, Kármán Tódor pedig a hangsebesség feletti repülést kutatta. Minél többet tudunk róluk, annál jobban értjük a huszadik századot.
b2-marslakok-consolidation.english: János Neumann studied the stored program, Leó Szilárd the chain reaction, Jenő Wigner symmetry principles, and Tódor Kármán flight above the speed of sound. The more we know about them, the better we understand the twentieth century.
b2-marslakok-consolidation.canDo: I can synthesize the biographies and scientific contributions of János Neumann, Leó Szilárd, Jenő Wigner, and Tódor Kármán.
